subject: Planning cadence: targets, signal windows, and ops handoff
messages:
From: Nikhil Sharma <nsharma@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kate Eastbrook <kate@eastbrook-advisors.com>, Acme Finance <procurement@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Planning cadence: targets, signal windows, and ops handoff

Team —

Kicking off a short working thread to align leadership + ops on the annual planning cadence and the handoff into QBR prep. High-level asks below; please read and react with any constraints by EOD Monday.

Ask / goals:
- Agree on 3 target bands (base / stretch / aggressive) and the signal windows that will move us between them.
- Lock the planning timeline so Product/Eng/CS can schedule planning work and customer outreach.
- Define the ops handoff: who owns the runbooks, playbooks for contingency triggers, and the A/B rollout windows for Dedicated capacity offers.

Attachments: planning timeline (spreadsheet) and scenario templates (PDF) — two working docs; expect edits.

Proposed timeline (attached sheet):
- Nov 5–12: leadership defines target bands + assumptions
- Nov 15–24: org-level scenario inputs (teams upload numbers into sheet)
- Dec 1: consolidated scenario review + QBR deck outline

Immediate asks (please):
1) Marissa — can you confirm Sales runrate assumptions and whether we should add a mid-cycle acceleration tranche?
2) Vivek — confirm whether exec QBR date of Dec 8 still holds for your calendar; if not propose alternatives.
3) Laura — any changes needed to forecasting model anchors for FY27?
4) Hannah/Monica — product & ops: who will be the single POC for post-decision rollout playbook?

If you want an in-person sync, I can block 30 minutes Monday, but prefer asynchronous edits first.

Thanks,
Nikhil Sharma
Head of Finance & Strategy
Redwood Inference

Attachments: 2026_planning_timeline_v1.xlsx; scenario_templates_v3.pdf
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nsharma@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Planning cadence: targets, signal windows, and ops handoff

Nikhil — thanks for kicking this off. Quick notes from Sales perspective: 

- Runrate assumptions: we should keep the current cohort-based funnel conversion but make two conservative adjustments for FY27: (1) slower mid-market conversion in Q1 due to product changes, (2) a small uplift from a new marketplace listing expected in Q2. I'll drop a tab in the timeline workbook with cohort-level assumptions by EOD Friday.
- Mid-cycle acceleration tranche: support adding an optional "growth tranche" that activates if pipeline coverage > 3.5x for two consecutive weeks. That gives us a clean trigger to fund go-to-market bursts without reforecasting the entire plan.

Operational ask: can we add a short column in the timeline for the expected communications plan (who emails customers, what channels)? That helps CS coordinate renewal windows.

Marissa Cole
VP, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachment: sales_assumptions_tab.xlsx (will be added to the drive)
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nsharma@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 11:20:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Planning cadence: targets, signal windows, and ops handoff

Quick calendar note — Dec 8 is tight for an in-person exec QBR because the SF office has a heavy scheduling window that week. Can we tentatively move the exec slot to Dec 10 (afternoon) or Dec 15 (AM)? Prefer Dec 10 if we can get buy-in.

On triggers: agree with Marissa's 3.5x pipeline trigger. I also want an explicit latency/cost SLO contingency: if median inference latency on Hosted API moves >15% for 72 hours, we automatically surface a capacity and pricing contingency assessment to the SLT. That should be in the ops handoff. Hannah/Monica — can you draft a 1-page runbook for that scenario?

Vivek Kulkarni
Chief Product Officer
Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nsharma@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 14:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Planning cadence: targets, signal windows, and ops handoff

Adding a couple of forecasting anchors: 
- Revenue recognition timing needs to be explicit in the scenario templates — for subscription deals that span quarters, please tag ARR vs recognized revenue so finance can prepare monthly P&L.
- Headcount assumptions: please flag any hiring freezes or planned headcount uplifts in the org-level inputs. That drives expense banding in the model.

I'll update the scenario_templates_v3.pdf with notes and upload a short example for how to tag deals in the timeline sheet.

Laura Bennett
VP, FP&A
Redwood Inference
From: Kate Eastbrook <kate@eastbrook-advisors.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nsharma@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 6 Nov 2026 16:28:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Planning cadence: targets, signal windows, and ops handoff

Nikhil / team — thanks for including Eastbrook. A quick ask from our side: we can run a short scenario stress-test on seeding Dedicated capacity discounts and quantify the margin impact across the three target bands. I can deliver a 2-pager by Nov 12 if you confirm the baseline SKU pricing to use (I propose current public list + 10% buffer for Feb chop).

Also, Acme Finance pinged asking whether the procurement timeline will need any special artifacts (SOC 2 evidence, custom SLA wording). If so, loop in Legal early — we can pre-seed language in the QBR prep deck.

Best,
Kate Eastbrook
Principal, Eastbrook Advisors (partner)
From: Nikhil Sharma <nsharma@redwood.ai>
To: Kate Eastbrook <kate@eastbrook-advisors.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 6 Nov 2026 16:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Planning cadence: targets, signal windows, and ops handoff

Kate — excellent, please go ahead on the stress test with the proposed baseline (public list + 10%). Marissa/Laura — we'll need the sales/ARR tagging in the timeline by Monday so Eastbrook can run the margin sensitivity.

On procurement: Laura, can you confirm what artifacts we'll surface to Acme (SOC2 + audit log summary)? If Legal needs to be looped, I'll add them to the thread.

I'll tentatively propose Dec 10 for the exec QBR and will block a 30-minute working session next Monday for leadership to review the assembled scenarios.

Thanks all — appreciate the quick turn.

Nikhil Sharma
Head of Finance & Strategy
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: 2026_planning_timeline_v1.xlsx; scenario_templates_v3.pdf
